rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permission to retaliate equally for defense of life and property is a profound reality that friends and foes alike must hear.
rows.anchor: if the oppressed Muslims retaliate on equal footing to defend their life and wealth, they have this permission

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression for matching retaliation is phrased in deference to mujānasah, or verbal correspondence.
rows.anchor: is used in deference to mujānasah as in

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word then marks a further enemy excess after Muslim self-defense, intended to suppress future defense; God promises rescue and believers can be assured of it.
rows.anchor: if because of some defensive measure adopted by the Muslims, the disbelievers commit a further excess against them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised help was given at the migration and later stated more explicitly when Muslims became a force in Madinah; the reader is directed to 22:39–40.
rows.anchor: Later when they became a force in Madī nah, these same words were stated very clearly

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s forgiveness and mercy counsel oppressed Muslims against hasty retaliation before its proper time; although entitled to defend themselves, they should reflect some divine mercy, since God wants them to mirror His attributes.
rows.anchor: God wants to see a reflection of His attributes in the Muslims

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s alternation of night and day demonstrates that He controls the universe and underwrites His promise to help.
rows.anchor: It is He Who enters the day into the night and vice versa and He is also one who hears and sees all

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God hears and sees the wrongdoers’ mischief, He cannot be detached from governance and must help those reforming the world against disorder.
rows.anchor: He is not deaf and blind so that He is unaware of the mischief caused by the wrongdoers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Helping the believers is no difficulty for God, who admits night into day and day into night.
rows.anchor: How can this be difficult for Him at all when He is able to admit the night into the day

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God can change day and night, He can dispel disbelief and illuminate the world with faith.
rows.anchor: He can surely obliterate the darkness of disbelief and make the world shine with the radiance of faith

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second argument is that only God controls the universe; beings invoked besides Him are false and fabricated, and stones or idols cannot be equated with Him.
rows.anchor: All those whom these people invoke besides Him are baseless and a mere deception; in fact, they are their own fabrications

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase Do you not see addresses each individual in a group separately.
rows.anchor: are meant to address each and every individual of a group separately

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The observable world is added to God’s attributes as evidence supporting the promise of help: just as rain unexpectedly revives barren land, God can send help despite adverse appearances.
rows.anchor: the testimony of the world around human beings is also added to His attributes

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is subtle in bringing plans to fruition unnoticed and all-aware of past and future, while people know only what is apparent.
rows.anchor: He makes His plans materialize in a way that no one has any inkling of them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reinforces that the heavens and earth belong to God and remain under His control, so no one can obstruct His intentions.
rows.anchor: everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him and is under His control

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attribute worthy of praise qualifies God’s self-sufficiency, so people do not despair of His benevolence: despite being self-sufficient, He is benevolent and present with everyone.
rows.anchor: reason was dispel any hopelessness in people because of God being self-sufficient

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human respite is a divine favor: the things of heaven and earth serve people by God’s command and would otherwise turn against them.
rows.anchor: Everything of the heavens and earth is serving them – without which they cannot survive – at God’s behest

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ship sails because God has placed it in human service, and the sky remains held up by His command; otherwise the ship would sink and the sky fall.
rows.anchor: the sailing of the ship in the sea is cited. It does so because God has put it in their service

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An annexing noun meaning lest is understood as suppressed before the following particle.
rows.anchor: An annexing noun to the effect

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These phenomena show that human comforts come from divine mercy, not merely human knowledge or scientific progress; moving one building block of the universe would bring the whole structure down.
rows.anchor: whatever human beings have in this world is not because of their own knowledge and scientific advancements

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse warns Quraysh not to demand punishment hastily: its delay reflects mercy, giving them time to mend their ways rather than any difficulty for God.
rows.anchor: it is because of His mercy and favour so that they are able to benefit from this and mend their ways

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning turns to the hereafter: people still face the consequences of their deeds, and the God who gives life and death will resurrect them; resurrection is no harder than the first creation.
rows.anchor: When creating the first time was not difficult for Him, how can it pose a difficulty the second time

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents are ungrateful because the Prophet’s message and the Qur’an are completely clear, leaving no genuine disagreement about them.
rows.anchor: there cannot be any two opinions about it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human being refers specifically to the Prophet’s rebellious opponents; general wording avoids addressing them directly, expresses aversion, and conveys regret and sorrow at their behavior.
rows.anchor: The word “human being” here refers to these rebellious opponents

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mansak, discussed at 22:34, means a community’s ways of worship, the outward form of divine law, and its principles.
rows.anchor: Here it is used for ways of worship, the apparent form of divine law and its principles

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi says Jews and Christians were siding openly with Quraysh and fueling the debate; the verse says each community has a prescribed law, which it should follow and accept when God changes it, thereby distinguishing the sincere.
rows.anchor: it was they who were actually fuelling the whole debate. For this reason, the verse refers to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Across successive messengers, changes to outward law reform innovators’ fabrications; sincere truth-seekers accept reform, while traditionalists cling to inherited views and debate against it.
rows.anchor: Those who were seekers of the truth, accepted this reform with full sincerity

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s opponents cling prejudicially to jāhiliyyah customs, so he should not be troubled by them or give them an opening for polemical debate; he should remain on the straight path and invite them, then leave them to themselves if they refuse.
rows.anchor: he should not give them any opportunity to engage in polemical debates with him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is compared with 2:148, where each community has a direction and people are urged to excel in good deeds.
rows.anchor: And for each there is a fixed a direction towards which it turns

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If opponents initiate debate, the Prophet should say that God knows what they do and will judge their disagreements on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: God will decide between you on the Day of Judgement in what you are differing

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should ignore them and entrust their matter to God because they act deliberately and cannot be persuaded by reasoning.
rows.anchor: They are intentionally playing pranks and are not ones who can be persuaded through reasoning

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although addressed to the Prophet, the verse’s rebuke is directed at his adversaries, who should entrust their case to the God who knows all things in heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: Though this verse addresses the Prophet (sws), however the rebuke found in every word of it is directed at his adversaries

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The written register intensifies the warning: these are not empty threats, since God has minutely recorded every person’s deeds.
rows.anchor: no one should think that all these are baseless warnings; everyone should know that God has a written record of every person’s deeds

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse answers doubts about preserving every person’s detailed record: although this exceeds human capacity, it is very easy for God.
rows.anchor: This might be a tall order for everyone but, as the last part of the verse says, this is

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is also compared with 5:48, which says each community has an ordained rule and path and urges people to excel in good deeds.
rows.anchor: For each of you, We have ordained a rule and path.

rows.speaker: some people
rows.claim: Some people read the cited passages as expressing tolerance toward Jews and Christians; Islahi rejects that reading and says they express aversion toward them.
rows.anchor: these verses do not portray any tolerance for the Jews and Christians, as some people have understood

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi’s preferred interpretation is that the cited verses express aversion toward Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: They actually express and declare aversion against them
